feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 0 (score 176) left the line on every s-bend and slalom trial with max_error at the 0.06 m floor and low oscillation (0.14 to 0.32), so the robot was reacting late, not jittering. Iteration 1 (score 389) moved the sensors to y 0.06 and narrowed the track to 0.10 m. That fixed the oval (19 of 20 finishes) but left the s-bend at 1.0 line loss per run with progress 0.43, and the slalom at 1.75 losses. Oscillation stayed low on every track (0.23 to 0.27), so there is no sign of jitter. For this candidate the Integrator raises kp to 2.8 to add turn authority, so please read any s-bend result as the joint effect of geometry and that gain. If the next race shows s-bend line_loss_events still at or near 1.0 with max_error at the 0.06 floor, the limit is turn authority rather than look-ahead. In that case try a narrower track, since oscillation has headroom. If the oval finish rate falls below about 0.9 or oval max_error rises above 0.05, the look-ahead has gone far enough, so keep y at 0.07 or step back toward 0.06 rather than pushing further forward. If the slalom still loses the line about 1.75 times per run, the 12 mm footprint may be too narrow to hold the line on alternating bends, so test a larger footprint.
requested_changes: If s-bend line_loss_events stay near 1.0 with max_error at the 0.06 m floor and steering_oscillation is below about 0.3, set wheel_track to 0.09 (min 0.08) for more turn authority, since iteration 1 gave oscillation 0.23 on the s-bend at 0.10 m.

If oval finish rate falls below about 0.9 or oval max_error rises above 0.05 (iteration 1 gave 19 of 20 finishes and max_error 0.035), keep sensor y at 0.06 or 0.065 rather than 0.07, because the extra look-ahead is adding lag.

If slalom line_loss_events remain near 1.75 (iteration 1), change sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 with the same x positions, so the footprint overlaps more and keeps the line in view through alternating bends.
